name: Jamf Pro
description: Jamf Pro is Apple-only device management software that lets IT teams deploy, configure, secure, and patch Mac, iPhone, iPad, and Apple TV devices without user interaction.
best_for: IT and security teams that exclusively or primarily manage Apple devices and want deep, Apple-native device management rather than a cross-platform UEM tool.
features: Zero-touch deployment for Mac, iPhone, iPad, and Apple TV, including BYOD
Smart Groups for dynamic device and user segmentation, with an AI Assistant to help navigate them
Blueprints built on Declarative Device Management to configure settings, commands, app installs, and restrictions across devices
Automated inventory collection of hardware, software, and security configuration details
App lifecycle management and Self Service+, so end users can install apps and updates themselves
Compliance benchmarks based on industry security baselines, plus remote security commands that don't require user interaction
Integrations with Microsoft (Entra, Power BI, Security Copilot, Sentinel), Google (Workspace, Cloud Identity, Chrome Enterprise), Okta, and hundreds of tools via the Jamf Marketplace
pros: Deep, Apple-native management (Declarative Device Management, zero-touch deployment) built specifically for Mac, iPhone, iPad, and Apple TV
Free trial available with no credit card required
More than 20 years focused solely on Apple device management, per Jamf's own company history
cons: Apple-only -- Jamf Pro itself does not manage Windows or Android devices

Jamf's published per-device pricing ($12.50/device/month for Mac, $5.75/device/month for mobile) is for the bundled "Jamf for Mac" and "Jamf for Mobile" packages that combine Jamf Pro with Jamf Connect and Jamf Protect, not a standalone Jamf Pro price, and every plan still requires contacting sales rather than checking out online

tiers.name: Jamf for Mac
tiers.notes: Bundle price for Jamf Pro, Jamf Connect, and Jamf Protect together (not Jamf Pro alone), billed annually with a 25-device minimum. Every plan requires contacting sales to purchase -- there is no self-serve checkout.

tiers.name: Jamf for Mobile
tiers.notes: Bundle price for Jamf Pro, Jamf Connect, and Jamf Protect together (not Jamf Pro alone), billed annually with a 25-device minimum. Jamf markets this bundle as covering iOS, iPadOS, visionOS, watchOS, tvOS, and Android -- that cross-platform mobile coverage is attributed to the bundle, not confirmed as a capability of Jamf Pro on its own.

alternatives.name: ManageEngine Endpoint Central
alternatives.description: ManageEngine Endpoint Central is a unified endpoint management platform covering Windows, macOS, Linux, iOS, Android, and Chrome OS from one console.
alternatives.best_for: IT teams managing a mixed fleet of Apple and non-Apple devices that want one cross-platform UEM console instead of an Apple-specific tool.
strengths: Bundled patch management, EDR, and asset management

alternatives.name: NinjaOne
alternatives.description: NinjaOne is a unified IT operations platform combining RMM, patch management, backup, remote access, and service-desk ticketing for IT teams and MSPs.
alternatives.best_for: IT teams and MSPs that need Windows/macOS/Linux RMM alongside basic mobile device management, not Apple-specific depth.
strengths: Single console for RMM, patching, and backup

faq.question: Does Jamf Pro manage Windows or Android devices?
faq.answer: No. Jamf Pro itself manages Apple devices only -- Mac, iPhone, iPad, and Apple TV. Cross-platform mobile support, including Android, is only mentioned by Jamf in the context of its bundled "Jamf for Mobile" package, which combines Jamf Pro with Jamf Connect and Jamf Protect.

faq.question: How much does Jamf Pro cost?
faq.answer: Jamf doesn't publish a standalone Jamf Pro price. Its pricing page shows bundle pricing starting at $12.50/Mac device/month or $5.75/mobile device/month (billed annually, 25-device minimum) for packages that include Jamf Pro plus Jamf Connect and Jamf Protect, and every plan requires contacting sales to purchase.
